QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_21

question.text: The listing of a Zero Coupon Zero Principal Instrument on the SSE will TERMINATE when which of the following conditions is met?

answer.text: The issuing NPO surrenders its Section 12A registration.
The NPO's audited accounts show the program cost exceeded the ZCZP subscription amount by more than 10%.
The Social Impact Fund subscriber redeems its units.

The object for which the funds were raised has been achieved AND a certificate to this effect is submitted to the SSE; OR the tenure to achieve the object as provided in the fund-raising document has expired.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.3, ZCZP listing terminates if (a) the object for which funds were raised has been achieved and a certificate to this effect is submitted to the SSE, OR (b) the tenure to achieve the object as provided in the fund-raising document has expired. These are the two statutory triggers. At termination, the instrument is written off the investee's books. The Trap: Option A is irrelevant to listing termination. Option C invents a cost-overrun trigger that does not exist. Option D reverses the role (SIF is subscriber; its redemption does not end the listing of the underlying ZCZP). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C/D/E treat scheme-termination triggers for AIFs, which are distinct. III-A/III-C treat delisting triggers on the main board. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When writing your completion-certificate assurance report, use the 'achievement-of-object' language tightly to the fund-raising document's stated deliverables — if the NPO has overachieved on some KPIs but underachieved on the stated object, the listing should NOT be terminated on achievement grounds; it simply runs until tenure expiry.
